name: Andorra
flagFacts: It combines elements from neighboring countries, using the blue and red of France alongside the red and yellow of Spain.
The central coat of arms features the historical mitre and crozier of the Bishop of Urgell, reflecting the country's unique co-principality status.

name: United Arab Emirates
flagFacts: The flag features the Pan-Arab colors of red, green, white, and black to symbolize regional unity.
The green vertical block represents prosperity, white represents peace, and black represents historical strength.

name: Afghanistan
flagFacts: The flag features the Shahada (Islamic declaration of faith) written in white text across the center.
The design historically changes frequently, making it one of the most altered national flags in modern history.

name: Antigua and Barbuda
flagFacts: The central rising sun symbolizes the dawn of a completely new era for the independent nation.
The distinct V-shape created by the red side panels stands for 'Victory' over colonial rule.

name: Albania
flagFacts: The double-headed black eagle traces its origins back to the medieval hero Skanderbeg, who used it as a seal in the 15th century.
The red field represents the bravery and blood spilled by the nation's soldiers throughout history.

name: Armenia
flagFacts: The bottom orange stripe is officially defined as symbolizing the talent, hard work, and resilience of the Armenian people.
The top red stripe represents the Armenian Highlands, the continuous struggle for survival, and the Christian faith.

name: Angola
flagFacts: The split red and black field represents the blood spilled during the anti-colonial struggle and the entire African continent.
The central emblem features a half-gear and a machete, intentionally mirroring the classic hammer and sickle to symbolize industry and agriculture.

name: Argentina
flagFacts: The light blue and white stripes were chosen by military leader Manuel Belgrano to match the colors of the Argentine revolution's cockades.
The central 'Sun of May' features alternating straight and wavy rays, modeled directly after an indigenous Incan representation of the sun god Inti.

name: Austria
flagFacts: Legend says the red and white pattern originated when Duke Leopold V's white tunic was entirely soaked in blood during a battle, except for the white strip under his belt.
It is officially recognized as one of the oldest continuously used national flag designs in the entire world.

name: Australia
flagFacts: The prominent Union Jack reflects the nation's historical constitutional links to the British monarchy.
The large seven-pointed Commonwealth Star has six points representing the original states, and a seventh point representing all internal and external territories.

name: Aruba
flagFacts: The four-pointed red star acts as a visual compass, representing the four major directions from which people migrated to populate the island.
The light blue field symbolizes the Caribbean Sea, bordered below by two yellow stripes that celebrate the historic gold rush and native flora colors.

name: Azerbaijan
flagFacts: The blue stripe represents the country's Turkic heritage, green represents Islam, and red symbolizes cultural modernization.
The central eight-pointed star stands for the eight historical branches of the Turkic peoples.

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
flagFacts: The stars are intentionally cut off at the top and bottom edges to imply an infinite continuation of the pattern.
The distinct yellow triangle represents both the approximate geographic shape of the country and the three main ethnic groups.

name: Barbados
flagFacts: The black trident head represents the mythical sea god Neptune and the nation's deep, historical connection to the ocean.
The trident's broken shaft symbolizes a permanent break from the country's past colonial ties with Great Britain.

name: Bangladesh
flagFacts: The red circle is offset slightly toward the hoist so that it appears perfectly centered when the flag is flying in the wind.
The green background represents the lush, vibrant landscape of the country, rather than standard Islamic symbolism.

name: Belgium
flagFacts: The unusual 13:15 ratio makes the flag appear almost square when flown at its official dimensions.
The black, yellow, and red colors were taken directly from the coat of arms of the historical Duchy of Brabant.

name: Burkina Faso
flagFacts: The red half symbolizes the socialist revolution, while the green half represents the nation's agricultural riches.
The central yellow star acts as a guiding light for the principles of the revolution.

name: Bulgaria
flagFacts: The white stripe symbolizes peace and freedom, green represents agricultural abundance, and red represents the blood shed for independence.
The flag previously featured a complex state emblem in the upper hoist corner during the communist era, which was completely removed in 1990.

name: Bahrain
flagFacts: The flag's five white serrated triangles form a zigzag edge that represents the Five Pillars of Islam.
Until 2002, the flag officially had eight points before being reduced to five to match the religious pillars.

name: Burundi
flagFacts: The three central stars represent the national motto: 'Unité, Travail, Progrès' (Unity, Work, Progress).
The stars also historically symbolize the three main ethnic groups living within the country: the Hutu, Tutsi, and Twa.

name: Benin
flagFacts: The green stripe represents hope and the lush southern forests, yellow represents the northern savannas, and red represents the blood of ancestors.
The layout was entirely abandoned during the communist era from 1975 to 1990 before being fully restored to symbolize democratic transition.

name: Bermuda
flagFacts: Unlike most British Overseas Territories that use a blue ensign, Bermuda uniquely uses a red ensign as the base field for its national flag.
The detailed coat of arms depicts a wrecked ship, the Sea Venture, which deliberately commemorates the historical 1609 crash that led to the island's human settlement.

name: Bolivia
flagFacts: The central coat of arms includes an Andean condor, an alpaca, a breadfruit tree, and a sheaf of wheat to showcase national wealth.
The military, state, and naval flags include the central emblem, but the standard civil flag used by citizens is a simple tricolor.

name: Brazil
flagFacts: The night sky inside the blue globe accurately depicts the stellar constellation over Rio de Janeiro on November 15, 1889, the day the republic was declared.
The national motto 'Ordem e Progresso' (Order and Progress) was directly inspired by French philosopher Auguste Comte's positivist maxim.

name: Bahamas
flagFacts: The black equilateral triangle on the hoist represents the unity, determination, and strength of the Bahamian population.
The aquamarine stripes symbolize the clear, surrounding waters of the Atlantic Ocean, while the gold stripe represents the sun-drenched sands.

name: Bhutan
flagFacts: The snarling white dragon is Druk, the Thunder Dragon, holding jewels in its claws to represent national wealth and security.
The yellow half represents civic tradition and imperial authority, while the orange half signifies the spiritual power of Drukpa Buddhism.

name: Botswana
flagFacts: The striking light blue field symbolizes life-giving rain, water, and the national motto 'Pula' (Let there be rain).
The black and white stripes represent racial harmony and unity, while mirroring the coat of arms of the native zebra.

name: Belarus
flagFacts: The unique vertical red-and-white pattern on the hoist is a traditional folk embroidery design woven from local flax.
The current flag is a direct modification of the Soviet-era design, simply removing the communist hammer, sickle, and star.

name: Belize
flagFacts: It is the only national flag in the world to prominently feature human beings as a core part of its central design.
The design depicts a mestizo and an Afro-Belizean man holding logging tools, referencing the nation's historical mahogany industry.

name: Canada
flagFacts: The stylized eleven-pointed maple leaf was specifically chosen because it does not correspond to any specific species of maple tree.
The red-white-red layout is based directly on the historical flag of the Royal Military College of Canada.

name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
flagFacts: The sky-blue field symbolizes peace, while the red diagonal stripe represents the blood shed by the country's martyrs.
The yellow star in the top left corner represents the bright future and potential of the nation.

name: Central African Republic
flagFacts: The design combines the blue, white, and red of France with the green, yellow, and red of the pan-African movement.
The single yellow star in the upper left corner guides the nation toward unity and freedom.

name: Switzerland
flagFacts: It is one of only two square national flags in the world, using an exact 1:1 aspect ratio.
The white cross on a red field originated as a military ensign used by the Old Swiss Confederacy in the 14th century.

name: Chile
flagFacts: The lone star acts as a guide to progress and honor, earning the flag its popular local nickname, 'La Estrella Solitaria.'
The white section represents the snow of the Andes mountains, while the blue represents the clear sky.

name: Cameroon
flagFacts: It was the second modern African nation to officially adopt the pan-African colors of green, red, and yellow.
The single yellow star in the middle is known as the 'Star of Unity' and symbolizes the unification of the country.

name: China
flagFacts: The largest gold star represents the ruling Communist Party of China.
The four smaller stars represent the four traditional social classes of the Chinese people, aligned to face the larger star in absolute unity.

name: Colombia
flagFacts: The top yellow stripe is double the width of the blue and red stripes combined, creating an asymmetrical layout.
The yellow represents the country's golden wealth, blue represents the two oceans it touches, and red represents the blood of independence heroes.

name: Costa Rica
flagFacts: The blue, white, and red horizontal stripes were explicitly inspired by the ideals of the French Revolution.
The version used for official state duties features a detailed coat of arms showing three active smoking volcanoes.

name: Cuba
flagFacts: The three blue stripes represent the three historical military departments into which Spanish colonial rule divided the island.
The white star inside the red triangle represents absolute independence and freedom from foreign rule.

name: Cyprus
flagFacts: The flag features a map of the island colored in copper, referencing the country's ancient copper mining history.
The design explicitly avoids using blue or red to remain completely neutral between Greek and Turkish communities.

name: Czechia
flagFacts: The blue wedge on the hoist was added to the original red and white stripes to represent the region of Moravia.
The flag is identical to the former flag of Czechoslovakia, which the country retained after the peaceful dissolution of the union.

name: Germany
flagFacts: The black, red, and gold colors originated from the uniforms of the Lützow Free Corps during the Napoleonic Wars.
The gold color is officially defined as 'gold' rather than yellow, a distinction protected by German constitutional tradition.

name: Djibouti
flagFacts: The light blue stripe represents the sea and the sky, while the green stripe represents the earth and the land.
The red star inside the white triangle symbolizes unity and the blood of the struggle for independence.

name: Denmark
flagFacts: According to national legend, the flag fell directly from heaven during the Battle of Lyndanisse in the year 1219.
It holds the official Guinness World Record for the oldest continuously used national flag design.

name: Dominica
flagFacts: It is one of only two national flags in the world to feature the color purple, found on the feathers of the sisserou parrot.
The ten green stars surrounding the parrot represent the ten parishes of the island.

name: Dominican Republic
flagFacts: It is the only national flag in the world that features a depiction of the Holy Bible within its central coat of arms.
The blue and red rectangles are arranged in an alternating checkerboard pattern divided by a prominent white cross.

name: Algeria
flagFacts: The white section signifies absolute peace, while the green half represents Islam and the beauty of nature.
The crescent and star are iconic Islamic symbols, with the deep red color explicitly honoring those who fell during the war of independence.

name: Ecuador
flagFacts: The central coat of arms depicts Mount Chimborazo, the highest mountain in the country, alongside the Guayas River.
The flag shares its yellow, blue, and red tricolor design with Colombia and Venezuela due to their shared history in Gran Colombia.

name: Estonia
flagFacts: The unique blue, black, and white color combination represents the sky, the dark soil, and the bright winter snow.
The flag's colors are deeply rooted in the landscape, reflecting the natural colors of the Estonian forests during winter.

name: Egypt
flagFacts: The central emblem is the Eagle of Saladin, a historical symbol of Arab unity and strength.
The white stripe represents the peaceful nature of the 1952 revolution, while the black stripe represents the dark period of colonial oppression.

name: Eritrea
flagFacts: The prominent red triangle represents the blood shed during the thirty-year war for independence.
The yellow olive wreath and branch design was inspired by the country's historical United Nations flag from 1952.

name: Spain
flagFacts: The yellow stripe is double the width of the two red stripes combined, a layout known as the Spanish fess.
The coat of arms features the Pillars of Hercules with the historical motto 'Plus Ultra' (Further Beyond).

name: Ethiopia
flagFacts: The green, yellow, and red color scheme became the original inspiration for the Pan-African flag colors across the continent.
The central blue disc features a yellow pentagram with radiating lines that represent unity, peace, and prosperity.

name: Finland
flagFacts: The blue Nordic cross represents the thousands of lakes dotting the country, while the white background represents winter snow.
The design is based on the Nordic cross pattern, showing the country's cultural alignment with Sweden and Denmark.

name: Fiji
flagFacts: The flag retains the British Union Jack in the upper left corner despite becoming a fully independent republic in 1970.
The light blue field symbolizes the vast Pacific Ocean, breaking away from standard British dark blue ensigns.

name: Micronesia
flagFacts: The blue field represents the Pacific Ocean, while the four white stars are arranged to mirror the geographic layout of the island states.
The four stars represent the constituent states of Chuuk, Pohnpei, Kosrae, and Yap.

name: Faroe Islands
flagFacts: Known locally as 'Merkið' (The Banner), the flag's design was originally hand-drawn by Faroese university students studying over in Copenhagen during 1919.
The dominant white field represents the intense sea foam crests, while the thin blue and red lines mirror the traditional native clothing styles.

name: France
flagFacts: The white stripe represents the historical monarchy, while the blue and red stripes represent the city colors of Paris.
The navy blue stripe was briefly lightened to match Europe's flag colors before being changed back to dark navy in 2020.

name: Gabon
flagFacts: The yellow stripe represents the equator, which passes directly through the territory of the nation.
The green stripe symbolizes the country's extensive forest cover, while the blue stripe represents the Atlantic Ocean.

name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
Grenada
flagFacts: The small symbol on the left hoist represents a clove of nutmeg, which is one of the island's most famous agricultural exports.
The seven stars on the red border represent the seven parishes of the island nation.

name: Georgia
flagFacts: The design features the central St. George's Cross alongside four smaller Bolnisi crosses in each quadrant.
The current design was used by the medieval Kingdom of Georgia before being revived as the official flag in 2004.

name: Guernsey
flagFacts: The flag features a distinct gold cross placed directly inside a larger red St. George's Cross, symbolizing Duke William of Normandy's historic banner at the Battle of Hastings.
Adopted in 1985, this layered layout was specifically designed to stop international observers from confusing Guernsey vessels with English ones at sea.

name: Ghana
flagFacts: The central black star was adopted from the shipping line of Marcus Garvey, symbolizing African freedom and independence.
It was the very first sub-Saharan African nation to adopt the red, gold, and green pan-African color palette.

name: Gibraltar
flagFacts: It is an elongated banner of arms based entirely on a royal warrant issued by Queen Isabella I of Castile way back in 1502.
The three-towered red castle and golden key represent Gibraltar's historic geopolitical role as the literal key to locking or unlocking the Mediterranean Sea.

name: Greenland
flagFacts: It is the only Nordic territory flag that completely rejects the traditional cross layout, opting instead for a striking split-disc design.
The large white and red semi-circles represent the massive polar ice caps and the sun setting over the surrounding Arctic ocean.

name: Gambia
flagFacts: The blue horizontal stripe represents the Gambia River, which flows directly through the center of the nation.
The thin white stripes bordering the blue line represent peace, purity, and national unity.

name: Guinea
flagFacts: The vertical tricolor design was explicitly modeled after the French flag, replacing the colors with African tones.
The red stripe represents the blood shed for freedom, yellow represents the sun and gold, and green represents the forests.

name: Equatorial Guinea
flagFacts: The central silk-cotton tree on the shield represents the historical spot where the first treaty was signed with Spain.
The blue triangle at the hoist symbolizes the sea that connects the mainland to the country's island territories.

name: Greece
flagFacts: The nine horizontal stripes represent the nine syllables of the traditional revolutionary motto, 'Eleutheria i Thanatos' (Freedom or Death).
The blue and white cross in the upper left corner symbolizes the nation's traditional Eastern Orthodox Christian faith.

name: South Georgia and South Sandwich Islands
Guatemala
flagFacts: The flag features the Resplendent Quetzal, the national bird that symbolizes liberty and independence.
The two vertical blue stripes represent the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea that flank the country.

name: Guam
flagFacts: The unique almond-shaped emblem in the center represents the shape of a traditional Chamorro hunting slingstone.
The interior scene depicts an unyielding lone coconut palm tree surviving a massive storm, symbolizing the ultimate resilience of the indigenous population.

name: Guinea-Bissau
flagFacts: The design incorporates the black star of Africa on a vertical red stripe, honoring the anti-colonial struggle.
The flag's layout and colors are based directly on the historical political party flag of the PAIGC.

name: Guyana
flagFacts: Known popularly as 'The Golden Arrowhead,' the design features a distinct golden triangle pointing toward the fly.
The green field represents the dense forests that cover roughly 80% of the country's territory.

name: Honduras
flagFacts: The five blue stars represent the five original member nations of the former Federal Republic of Central America.
In 2022, the government officially changed the shade of the blue stripes from dark navy to a historical turquoise.

name: Croatia
flagFacts: The central shield features a red and white checkerboard pattern known as the 'sahovnica,' which dates back to medieval times.
The crown above the shield holds five historical regional coats of arms representing Croatia, Dubrovnik, Dalmatia, Istria, and Slavonia.

name: Haiti
flagFacts: The central coat of arms features a palm tree topped by a liberty cap, surrounded by hidden military trophies.
Legend says the flag was created by ripping the white center out of the French tricolor during the anti-colonial revolution.

name: Hungary
flagFacts: The horizontal red, white, and green stripes were officially adopted during the revolutions of 1848 to represent national freedom.
The red symbolizes strength, white symbolizes fidelity, and green symbolizes hope for the nation's future.

name: Indonesia
flagFacts: The flag is visually identical to the flag of Monaco, leading to a long-standing historical dispute between the two nations.
The red and white colors trace back to the banner of the medieval Majapahit Empire in the 13th century.

name: Ireland
flagFacts: The green stripe represents the Catholic population, orange represents the Protestant population, and white symbolizes permanent peace between them.
The flag was originally presented as a gift to Thomas Francis Meagher in 1848 by a group of sympathetic French women.

name: Israel
flagFacts: The blue stripes are designed to mirror the traditional Jewish prayer shawl known as the tallit.
The central blue hexagram is the Star of David, a universally recognized symbol of Jewish identity and culture.

name: India
flagFacts: The central wheel is the Ashoka Chakra, a 24-spoke wheel representing the eternal law of righteousness and duty.
The flag must legally be made from 'khadi,' a specific type of hand-spun cloth popularized by Mahatma Gandhi.

name: Iraq
flagFacts: The central green Arabic script reads 'Allahu Akbar' (God is Great) and was added during the Gulf War period.
The font style of the script was changed from Saddam Hussein's personal handwriting to a traditional Kufic script in 2008.

name: Iran
flagFacts: The words 'Allahu Akbar' (God is Great) are written 22 times in Kufic script along the edges of the green and red stripes.
The central emblem is a highly stylized composite symbol that spells out the word 'Allah' in the shape of a tulip.

name: Iceland
flagFacts: The red cross inside the white cross symbolizes the active volcanic fires of the island cutting through the winter ice.
The flag uses the classic Nordic cross layout to reflect its deep cultural and historical ties to Scandinavia.

name: Italy
flagFacts: The tricolor design was heavily inspired by the French flag following Napoleon's military campaigns across the peninsula.
The green stripe represents the country's plains and hills, white represents the snow of the Alps, and red represents the blood of wars.

name: Jersey
flagFacts: The red diagonal cross (saltire) was officially paired with the golden crest of three leopards in 1981 to clearly distinguish Jersey's flag from international maritime signal flags.
The golden Plantagenet crown atop the central shield was personally approved by Queen Elizabeth II to honor the island's historical loyalty to the English monarchy.

name: Jamaica
flagFacts: It is currently the only national flag in the world that does not contain any of the colors red, white, or blue.
The gold diagonal cross, or saltire, divides the flag into four distinct triangles of green and black.

name: Jordan
flagFacts: The white seven-pointed star represents the seven verses of the Al-Fatiha, the opening chapter of the Holy Quran.
The black, white, and green stripes represent the historical Abbasid, Umayyad, and Fatimid Islamic caliphates.

name: Kenya
flagFacts: The central Maasai shield and two crossed spears symbolize the defense of national freedom and sovereignty.
The thin white stripes were added to the original political party flag to symbolize peace and unity among ethnic groups.

name: Kyrgyzstan
flagFacts: The central red circle features a stylized depiction of a 'tunduk,' the traditional crown of a Kyrgyz yurt tent.
The sun has exactly forty rays, representing the forty historical tribes united by the legendary national hero Manas.

name: Cambodia
flagFacts: It is currently the only national flag in the world to feature a realistic depiction of an actual building: Angkor Wat.
The blue stripes represent royalty, while the red field represents the common people and national bravery.

name: Kiribati
flagFacts: The flag features a frigatebird flying over a rising sun and seventeen rhythmic, undulating blue and white ocean waves.
The seventeen waves represent the sixteen Gilbert Islands plus the single isolated island of Banaba.

name: Comoros
flagFacts: The four horizontal colored stripes represent the four main islands of the archipelago: Grande Comore, Mohéli, Anjouan, and Mayotte.
The four stars inside the green triangle also match the islands, even though Mayotte remains under French administration.

name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
flagFacts: The two green triangles represent the fertile land, while the black diagonal stripe represents the African heritage of the people.
The two white stars symbolize liberty and hope, while representing the two main islands that form the federation.

name: The Democratic People's Republic of Korea
Kuwait
flagFacts: The trapezoid shape on the hoist is black, representing the battlefields, while the green stripe represents the fertile lands.
The colors are derived from a historical poem by Safie Al-Deen Al-Hali describing Arab actions and history.

name: Kazakhstan
flagFacts: The ornamental pattern along the hoist is a traditional Kazakh design representing the culture and art of the steppe.
The golden sun features 32 rays shaped like grain to symbolize abundance, with a soaring steppe eagle beneath it.

name: Lebanon
flagFacts: The central green Cedar of Lebanon is a biblical symbol representing holiness, eternity, and national peace.
The top and bottom red stripes symbolize the blood shed to protect the country from successive foreign invaders.

name: Saint Lucia
flagFacts: The central triangles represent the Twin Pitons, two dramatic volcanic spires that rise directly out of the ocean.
The bright yellow triangle symbolizes the tropical sunshine and the island's thriving tourism industry.

name: Liechtenstein
flagFacts: The gold crown was added in 1937 after the country realized its flag was identical to Haiti's flag at the 1936 Olympics.
The blue field represents the sky, while the red field represents the glowing embers of evening fires.

name: Sri Lanka
flagFacts: The prominent golden lion holding a sword represents the Sinhalese ethnicity and the bravery of the nation.
The four bo leaves in the corners represent the four Buddhist virtues of kindness, compassion, joy, and equanimity.

name: Liberia
flagFacts: The flag is closely modeled after the flag of the United States, reflecting the country's founding by freed American slaves.
The eleven stripes represent the eleven signatories of the Liberian Declaration of Independence in 1847.

name: Lesotho
flagFacts: The central design features a traditional 'mokorotlo,' a conical straw hat that serves as an iconic symbol of Basotho culture.
The blue stripe represents rain, white represents peace, and green represents the agricultural prosperity of the nation.

name: Lithuania
flagFacts: The yellow stripe represents the golden sun and agricultural fields, green represents the forests, and red represents the blood of patriots.
The flag's colors were chosen by a special committee in 1918 to incorporate traditional Lithuanian folk weaving tones.

name: Luxembourg
flagFacts: The flag is almost identical to the flag of the Netherlands, but uses a longer aspect ratio and a lighter shade of sky blue.
The colors are derived from the 13th-century coat of arms of the Grand Duke, which featured a red lion on blue and white stripes.

name: Latvia
flagFacts: Legend states the flag originated from a white sheet used to carry a wounded warrior, where his blood stained the outer edges red.
The unique shade of deep red is internationally recognized and specifically designated as 'Latvian red.'

name: Libya
flagFacts: Between 1977 and 2011, Libya used a completely plain, solid green flag, making it the world's only monochrome national flag at the time.
The current design restores the historical 1951 independence flag, featuring the white crescent and star of Cyrenaica.

name: Morocco
flagFacts: The central green pentagram is the Seal of Solomon, representing the connection between God and the nation.
The solid red field has been used by the ruling Alaouite dynasty as a historical symbol since the 17th century.

name: Monaco
flagFacts: The red and white colors are the heraldic colors of the House of Grimaldi, which has ruled the principality since the 13th century.
The flag shares its exact color layout with the flag of Indonesia, differing only in its technical aspect ratio.

name: Moldova
flagFacts: The central emblem features a traditional auerox (wild bull) head holding a crescent, a star, and a flower between its horns.
The blue, yellow, and red vertical tricolor is shared with Romania, reflecting the deep cultural and historical ties between the nations.

name: Montenegro
flagFacts: The flag features a double-headed golden eagle holding a scepter and an orb, representing the historical unity of church and state.
The design is bordered entirely by a golden frame, setting it apart from most standard European tricolors.

name: Madagascar
flagFacts: The vertical white stripe represents purity and integrity, while the red and green stripes represent independence and hope.
The red and white colors were taken from the historical banners of the Merina Kingdom that ruled the island before colonization.

name: Marshall Islands
flagFacts: The diagonal orange and white bands represent the two major island chains within the nation: Ratak (sunrise) and Ralik (sunset).
The large star features 24 points representing the electoral districts, with four longer points pointing to the principal sub-centers.

name: North Macedonia
flagFacts: The flag features a golden sun with eight widening rays extending to the edges, known as the 'Sun of Liberty.'
The design was adopted in 1995 to resolve an intense diplomatic dispute with Greece over the historical Vergina Sun symbol.

name: Mali
flagFacts: The vertical tricolor uses the classic pan-African colors of green, yellow, and red to signify solidarity with the continent.
The flag previously featured a black human stick figure called a kanaga in the center, which was removed in 1961 due to religious objections.

name: Mongolia
flagFacts: The left stripe features the 'Soyombo' symbol, a complex geometric column representing fire, sun, moon, earth, and water.
The blue central stripe represents the eternal blue sky, which is a core concept in traditional Mongolian spiritual culture.

name: Mauritania
flagFacts: The two red stripes at the top and bottom were added to the historical green flag in 2017 to honor independence sacrifices.
The emerald green field and gold crescent moon are traditional symbols representing the country's deep Islamic heritage.

name: Malta
flagFacts: The George Cross medal in the upper hoist was awarded to the entire population by King George VI for bravery during World War II.
The red and white colors date back to the historic standard of Count Roger I of Sicily in the 11th century.

name: Mauritius
flagFacts: Known as the 'Four Bands,' the flag features red, blue, yellow, and green horizontal stripes.
The blue stripe represents the Indian Ocean, while the yellow stripe represents the bright light of independence.

name: Maldives
flagFacts: The large green rectangle represents peace, prosperity, and the countless coconut palms that grow on the islands.
The red border serves as a stark reminder of the blood spilled by national heroes defending sovereignty.

name: Malawi
flagFacts: The red rising sun symbolizes the dawn of freedom and hope for the continent of Africa after colonial rule.
The black stripe represents the African people, red represents the blood of martyrs, and green represents nature.

name: Mexico
flagFacts: The central emblem depicts an Aztec legend where an eagle perched on a cactus devours a snake, marking where to build Tenochtitlan.
The green stripe represents hope, white represents unity, and red represents the blood of national heroes.

name: Malaysia
flagFacts: Known as the 'Jalur Gemilang' (Stripes of Glory), the flag features fourteen stripes representing the member states and federal territories.
The fourteen points on the star match the stripes, symbolizing the unified government of the Malaysian federation.

name: Mozambique
flagFacts: It is one of the few national flags in the world to feature a modern assault rifle (an AK-47) in its emblem.
The open book behind the rifle represents education, while the hoe represents the nation's agricultural workers.

name: Namibia
flagFacts: The golden sun features twelve individual rays representing the diverse ethnic groups and communities living in the nation.
The blue triangle represents the sky and the Atlantic Ocean, while the green triangle represents agricultural wealth.

name: Niger
flagFacts: The central orange disc represents the sun and the sacrifices made by the people during the struggle for independence.
The top orange stripe represents the Sahara Desert, while the bottom green stripe represents the fertile southern lands.

name: Nigeria
flagFacts: The design was created by an engineering student named Michael Akinkunmi, who won a nationwide competition in 1959.
The two green vertical bands represent agriculture, while the white band represents permanent peace.

name: Nicaragua
flagFacts: The central coat of arms features a rainbow that symbolizes peace and a liberty cap that signifies freedom.
The two blue stripes represent the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea, which frame the central landmass.

name: Netherlands
flagFacts: It is recognized as the oldest horizontal tricolor flag in continuous use, originating during the 16th-century revolt against Spain.
The top stripe was originally orange (the Prince's Flag) before being permanently changed to red due to the instability of orange dye.

name: Norway
flagFacts: Designed in 1821, it was the very first Nordic cross flag to introduce a distinct third color (blue) into the traditional cross layout.
The red, white, and blue colors were deliberately chosen to mirror the democratic colors of France and the United States.

name: Nauru
flagFacts: The horizontal yellow line represents the equator, which sits exactly one degree north of the island's actual geographic position.
The 12-pointed star represents the twelve original indigenous tribes that inhabited the island.

name: New Zealand
flagFacts: The flag features the Southern Cross constellation, using four red stars outlined in white to indicate its location in the South Pacific.
The country held a nationwide multi-stage referendum in 2015-2016 to change the flag design, but citizens voted to retain the original.

name: Oman
flagFacts: The emblem in the upper hoist shows a traditional 'khanjar' dagger sheathed over two crossed swords.
The white stripe represents peace, green represents the Green Mountains, and red represents battles against foreign invaders.

name: Panama
flagFacts: The flag is divided into four distinct quadrants of blue, white, and red to represent the political parties at the time of independence.
The blue star represents civic purity and honesty, while the red star represents authority and law.

name: Peru
flagFacts: Legend says the red and white colors were inspired by a flock of flamingos taking flight when General San Martín arrived.
The state version includes a coat of arms featuring a vicuña, a cinchona tree, and a cornucopia spilling gold coins.

name: French Polynesia
flagFacts: The central emblem features a traditional double-hulled outrigger sailing canoe, representing a sacred ancestral connection to epic ocean navigation.
The five distinct human figures riding inside the canoe emblem represent the five major island groups that form the archipelago territory.

name: Papua New Guinea
flagFacts: The flag design was created by a 15-year-old schoolgirl named Susan Karike in a nationwide art competition in 1971.
The upper half features a stylized Raggiana bird-of-paradise soaring across a dramatic black and red background.

name: Philippines
flagFacts: The flag is flown with the red stripe on top during times of war and the blue stripe on top during times of peace.
The eight rays of the central golden sun represent the first eight provinces that revolted against Spanish colonial rule.

name: Pakistan
flagFacts: The large white vertical stripe on the hoist represents the religious minorities living peacefully within the nation.
The green field and white crescent moon are classic Islamic symbols representing progress, light, and guidance.

name: Poland
flagFacts: The white and red horizontal stripes are derived from the historical coat of arms featuring a white eagle on a red shield.
The colors are legally protected and have specific mathematical coordinates defined in the Polish constitution.

name: Puerto Rico
flagFacts: The design shares an identical layout with the Cuban flag, but completely reverses the red and blue colors to show revolutionary solidarity between the islands.
For over four decades in the 20th century, displaying or owning this specific flag was classified as an illegal felony under local anti-sedition laws.

name: Portugal
flagFacts: The green section represents hope for the future, while the red section represents the blood spilled during the 1910 revolution.
The central design features an armillary sphere, an old navigational instrument honoring the golden age of Portuguese maritime exploration.

name: Palau
flagFacts: The golden disc represents the full moon, which is culturally seen as a symbol of peace, fertility, and celebration.
The moon is offset slightly toward the hoist so that it appears perfectly centered when the flag is flying in the wind.

name: Paraguay
flagFacts: It is unique among national flags because the front side (obverse) and back side (reverse) feature completely different emblems.
The front side displays the national coat of arms, while the reverse side displays the Treasury Seal with a lion guarding a liberty cap.

name: Qatar
flagFacts: It is the only national flag in the world that is more than twice as wide as it is high, using a unique 11:28 ratio.
The nine white points of the serrated edge mark Qatar as the ninth member of the 'reconciled Emirates' following a 1916 treaty.

name: Romania
flagFacts: The vertical blue, yellow, and red tricolor was inspired by the banners used during the Wallachian uprising of 1821.
The flag is visually identical to the flag of Chad, a situation that has led to official discussions at the United Nations.

name: Serbia
flagFacts: The coat of arms features a double-headed white eagle holding a shield with the Serbian cross and four Cyrillic firesteels.
The flag uses a reverse order of the Russian tricolor, placing red at the top, blue in the middle, and white at the bottom.

name: Russia
flagFacts: The white, blue, and red horizontal tricolor was originally introduced by Peter the Great as a merchant shipping ensign.
The color layout became the historical foundation for the Pan-Slavic colors adopted by many Eastern European nations.

name: Rwanda
flagFacts: The flag was completely redesigned in 2001 to promote national unity and move away from symbols associated with the 1994 genocide.
The bright yellow sun in the upper right corner features twenty-four rays that symbolize enlightenment and transparency.

name: Saudi Arabia
flagFacts: The flag features the Shahada (Islamic creed) written in Thuluth script above a horizontal unsheathed sword.
Because the sacred text is written on both sides, the flag is manufactured by sewing two separate pieces of cloth together.

name: Solomon Islands
flagFacts: The five white stars represent the five original island districts that formed the nation at independence.
The thin yellow diagonal stripe represents the tropical sunshine, separating the blue ocean from the green land.

name: Seychelles
flagFacts: The flag features five oblique colored bands radiating from the bottom corner to symbolize a dynamic nation moving into the future.
The yellow band represents the sun, red represents the people, white represents justice, and green represents the land.

name: Sudan
flagFacts: The green triangle at the hoist represents Islam, agricultural wealth, and the historical prosperity of the land.
The white stripe symbolizes peace and light, while the black stripe represents the name of the country itself.

name: Sweden
flagFacts: The yellow Nordic cross layout was directly inspired by the design of the Danish flag.
The blue and gold colors trace their origins back to King Magnus Ladulås's royal coat of arms in 1275.

name: Singapore
flagFacts: The crescent moon represents a young, rising nation, while the five stars represent the ideals of democracy, peace, progress, justice, and equality.
Red symbolizes universal brotherhood and equality, while white signifies everlasting purity and virtue.

name: Slovenia
flagFacts: The coat of arms depicts Mount Triglav, the highest peak in the country, beneath three golden six-pointed stars.
The wavy blue lines at the bottom of the shield represent the country's local rivers and the Adriatic Sea.

name: Slovakia
flagFacts: The central shield features a double white cross standing on the highest of three blue volcanic mountain peaks.
The coat of arms was added to the standard Slavic tricolor in 1992 to prevent confusion with the flag of Russia.

name: Sierra Leone
flagFacts: The horizontal green stripe represents agriculture, white represents unity, and blue represents the natural harbor of Freetown.
The simple tricolor layout was officially adopted upon gaining independence from Great Britain in 1961.

name: San Marino
flagFacts: The central coat of arms features three towers topped with feathers, representing the historical citadels built on Mount Titano.
The white stripe represents peace, while the light blue stripe represents the liberty of the ancient republic.

name: Senegal
flagFacts: The green, yellow, and red vertical bands feature the traditional pan-African colors to show regional solidarity.
The central five-pointed green star represents human spiritual openness and the five continents of the world.

name: Somalia
flagFacts: The light blue color was chosen as a direct tribute to the United Nations for assisting the country's transition to independence.
The single white star in the center is the Star of Unity, representing the historical regions inhabited by the Somali people.

name: Suriname
flagFacts: The central golden five-pointed star represents the unity of all ethnic groups that make up the population.
The red stripe symbolizes progress and love, while the green stripes represent agricultural abundance.

name: South Sudan
flagFacts: The black stripe represents the people, red represents the blood shed for freedom, and green represents the agricultural land.
The gold star inside the blue triangle represents the guiding light of Bethlehem and the unity of the states.

name: El Salvador
flagFacts: The central coat of arms contains five volcanoes rising from the sea, representing the five original states of the Central American provinces.
The words 'República de El Salvador en la América Central' are written in a circular pattern around the emblem.

name: Eswatini
flagFacts: The flag prominently displays a traditional Nguni shield, two spears, and a staff decorated with bird feathers.
The black and white coloring of the shield represents racial harmony and peaceful coexistence.

name: Chad
flagFacts: Its blue, yellow, and red tricolor is identical to the flag of Romania, causing occasional international vexillological disputes.
The blue stripe was originally intended to be green, but was changed to avoid confusion with neighboring African nations.

name: Togo
flagFacts: The five horizontal stripes represent the five distinct administrative regions of the country.
The single white star inside the red canton symbolizes life, liberty, and the independence of the nation.

name: Thailand
flagFacts: Known as the 'Trairanga' (Tricolor), the flag features five horizontal stripes of red, white, and blue.
The central blue stripe represents the monarchy, framed by white for religion and red for the nation's people.

name: Tajikistan
flagFacts: The central gold crown features an arc of seven stars, representing the seven historical cultural regions of the nation.
The red stripe represents the working class, white represents cotton production, and green represents agricultural land.

name: Turkmenistan
flagFacts: The vertical stripe features five intricate carpet designs, making it the most detailed national flag pattern in the world.
The two olive branches at the bottom of the stripe symbolize the country's officially recognized status of permanent neutrality.

name: Tunisia
flagFacts: The red crescent moon and star are historical symbols reflecting the nation's past ties to the Ottoman Empire.
The flag's layout has remained virtually unchanged since it was first designed by Ahmad I ibn Mustafa in 1831.

name: Tonga
flagFacts: The red cross in the white canton represents the nation's deep historical connection to Christianity.
The constitution explicitly states that the national flag can never be altered or changed under any circumstances.

name: Turkey
flagFacts: According to national legend, the design reflects the reflection of the crescent moon and a star in a pool of soldiers' blood.
The exact geometric proportions of the crescent and star are strictly protected by a dedicated national law.

name: Trinidad and Tobago
flagFacts: The black diagonal stripe represents the dedication of the people linked together by the ultimate bond of hard work.
The white borders symbolize the sea that surrounds the two main islands forming the nation.

name: Tuvalu
flagFacts: The light blue field features nine yellow stars that accurately mirror the geographical positions of the nation's nine islands.
The flag retains the British Union Jack in the upper left corner to acknowledge its ties to the Commonwealth.

name: Tanzania
flagFacts: The diagonal green stripe represents the land's vegetation, while the blue stripe represents the Indian Ocean.
The flag was created by merging the separate design elements of Tanganyika and Zanzibar following their union.

name: Ukraine
flagFacts: The blue stripe represents the clear sky, while the yellow stripe represents the vast golden wheat fields beneath it.
The simple horizontal layout became a powerful symbol of national sovereignty during the independence movement.

name: Uganda
flagFacts: The central grey crowned crane is a neutral symbol chosen because it was not used by any historical local kingdoms.
The black stripes represent the African people, yellow represents sunshine, and red represents brotherhood.

name: Uruguay
flagFacts: The flag features nine horizontal stripes representing the nine original departments created within the country.
The upper left corner features the Sun of May, a symbol of freedom celebrating the independence revolution.

name: Uzbekistan
flagFacts: The twelve stars represent the twelve constellations of the zodiac and the historical months of the traditional calendar.
The thin red stripes represent the vital forces of life flowing through the territory of the nation.

name: Vatican City
flagFacts: It is one of only two square national flags in the world, designed with a strict 1:1 aspect ratio.
The yellow half features the crossed keys of Saint Peter topped by the papal tiara, representing spiritual authority.

name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
flagFacts: The three green diamonds are arranged in the shape of the letter 'V' to stand for the first letter of the nation's name.
The blue stripe represents the sky, gold represents the sand, and green represents the lush tropical vegetation.

name: Venezuela
flagFacts: The arc of eight gold stars represents the eight historical provinces that signed the act of independence.
The eighth star was officially added to the design in 2006 to fulfill a historical decree by Simón Bolívar.

name: Vanuatu
flagFacts: The golden emblem features a curved boar's tusk, a traditional symbol of prosperity and wealth on the islands.
Two crossed namele fern leaves inside the tusk represent peace and compliance with traditional local laws.

name: Samoa
flagFacts: The upper left canton features five white stars representing the Southern Cross constellation, highlighting its Southern Hemisphere location.
The red field symbolizes courage, while the blue rectangle represents freedom and the surrounding ocean.

name: Yemen
flagFacts: The simple red, white, and black tricolor layout is based directly on the historical Arab Liberation Flag.
The flag was officially adopted in 1990 when North Yemen and South Yemen unified into a single state.

name: South Africa
flagFacts: Designed in 1994, it was intentionally created to have no official symbolic meaning for individual colors, allowing people to find personal meaning.
The distinct Y-shape converging into a single horizontal band symbolizes the convergence of diverse groups into a unified nation.

name: Zambia
flagFacts: The orange eagle soaring in the upper right corner represents the people's ability to rise above national problems.
The vertical blocks of green, red, black, and orange are uniquely placed on the fly side instead of the hoist.

name: Zimbabwe
flagFacts: The white triangle features the iconic Zimbabwe Bird emblem, modeled after soapstone carvings found at the ancient ruins of Great Zimbabwe.
The red star behind the bird symbol represents the revolutionary struggle and the path to peace.
